title: Secure Credential and Secret Vault Layer
summary: Manage credentials through encrypted versions, scoped short-lived leases, registered tool materialisation and metadata-only audit evidence.

intent.statement: Prevent credentials from entering model context, UI responses, logs, task state and ordinary APIs while enabling governed tools and workloads to use short-lived scoped secret material.
desired_outcomes: All secret values are encrypted through an approved key-management boundary.
Agents receive opaque capabilities at most and never plaintext secrets.
Every lifecycle or access decision is reconstructable with metadata-only evidence.

success_measures.name: Secret exposure prevention
success_measures.target: 0 plaintext values in approved API, task, log, audit and test fixtures
success_measures.measurement_method: Security tests, redaction scans and code review of vault boundaries.

success_measures.name: Lease policy coverage
success_measures.target: 100% secret materialisations have short-lived policy-approved lease evidence
success_measures.measurement_method: Reconcile registered tool materialisation attempts with lease and ledger records.

problem.statement: AI-native engineering workflows create an elevated risk of credential leakage when secrets are handled as ordinary configuration or agent context.
problem.current_state: AGASTYA defines agent, tool and ledger controls but no dedicated vault contract for encrypted storage, opaque delivery, rotation or revocation.
impact: Credentials could leak through prompts, logs or tool output.
Agents could gain broader access than the task requires.
Revocation and rotation evidence could be incomplete.

business_context.business_value: A vault boundary permits safe integration and controlled agents without normalising secret exposure as part of engineering workflows.

stakeholders.name: Security Engineering
stakeholders.role: Owns key-management and access policy review

stakeholders.name: Platform Engineering
stakeholders.role: Owns vault integration and tool materialisation

actors.name: Project Owner
goals: Manage secret metadata and approve sensitive lifecycle actions.

actors.name: Vault Service
goals: Validate policy and issue opaque short-lived leases.

actors.name: Registered Tool Workload
goals: Materialise a granted secret only at execution boundary.

actors.name: AI Agent
goals: Request a secret-backed tool action without observing secret value.

functional_requirements.title: Define scoped secret metadata
functional_requirements.statement: The system shall create project-scoped SecretDefinitions with type, classification, owner, environment, consumer, access and rotation policy metadata.

functional_requirements.title: Write encrypted immutable secret versions
functional_requirements.statement: The system shall write immutable encrypted SecretVersions through an approved key-management provider adapter and retain only audit-safe fingerprint and metadata in AGASTYA records.

functional_requirements.title: Prohibit normal plaintext retrieval
functional_requirements.statement: The system shall return metadata only through normal secret APIs and deny plaintext read or export requests.

functional_requirements.title: Issue bound short-lived secret leases
functional_requirements.statement: The system shall issue a short-lived SecretLease only to a registered tool or workload after scope, environment, purpose, state, policy and approval checks.

functional_requirements.title: Inject secrets outside agent context
functional_requirements.statement: The system shall materialise secret values directly at registered tool or workload execution boundary without exposing them to agent prompts, task records, tool responses or UI.

functional_requirements.title: Rotate and revoke secret versions
functional_requirements.statement: The system shall activate, rotate, retire, revoke and destroy versions through governed lifecycle actions and metadata-only audit events.

non_functional_requirements.statement: Secret plaintext shall not appear in normal API responses, UI views, model context, task state, logs, ledger payloads or error messages.
non_functional_requirements.verification_method: End-to-end test and redaction scan inspect API, task, tool, log and audit fixtures after write and materialisation flows.
non_functional_requirements.target: Zero recoverable plaintext occurrences in approved test surfaces.

non_functional_requirements.statement: Revocation shall block new leases immediately and active leases shall be invalidated or expire according to registered provider and target capability.
non_functional_requirements.verification_method: Integration tests revoke active and inactive versions then assert denied new grants and recorded active-lease outcome.
non_functional_requirements.target: No new lease issued for revoked version.

business_rules.statement: Normal application, UI, API and agent paths may never return or display a secret plaintext value.
exceptions: Registered tool/workload execution boundary may materialise a value under an approved short-lived lease without returning it to caller.

business_rules.statement: A lease is bound to one secret version, project, environment, registered consumer, purpose and expiry and cannot be transferred or renewed without policy re-evaluation.
An agent may receive only an opaque secret capability reference and may not receive plaintext, ciphertext, raw bearer token or reusable provider credential in its context or output.

constraints.statement: AGASTYA shall delegate root-key operations and cryptographic primitives to an approved KMS/HSM or managed secret provider and shall not implement custom cryptography.
constraints.rationale: Root-key management and cryptographic implementation require specialised, independently reviewed controls.

dependencies.name: Approved key-management service
dependencies.risk: Provider selection, data residency and root-key operating model are pending security architecture decision.

bounded_contexts.name: Secret and Credential Management
bounded_contexts.responsibility: Own secret metadata, encrypted versions, policy evaluation, leases, lifecycle, provider adapters and safe audit metadata.

ubiquitous_language.definition: Project-scoped metadata and policy describing a credential without its value.
One immutable encrypted credential value with lifecycle and fingerprint metadata.
Short-lived, bound permission to materialise one active version at registered execution boundary.

workflows.name: Materialise secret for registered tool
workflows.trigger: A policy-approved tool task requires an authorised secret-backed operation.

steps.action: Resolves project, active version, environment, registered consumer, purpose and policy.
steps.result: Lease is denied, blocked for approval or granted with bounded expiry.

steps.action: Materialises value only at execution boundary using the opaque lease.
steps.result: Tool operates without returning credential to agent or caller.

steps.action: Records lease and result metadata in the evidence ledger.
steps.result: Use is auditable without secret material.

outcomes: Approved tool uses scoped credential without agent visibility.
workflows.error_handling: Policy denial, expired/revoked version or provider failure returns no secret material and creates metadata-only evidence.

states.name: DESTROYED
states.description: Provider and retention policy approved destruction.

security_requirements.statement: Every secret operation shall enforce project scope, classification, authenticated identity or workload, action policy and metadata-only audit logging.
security_requirements.verification_method: Security test matrix covers wrong project, unauthorised role, tool mismatch, environment mismatch, expired lease and plaintext export attempt.

observability_requirements.statement: Secret lifecycle, policy, lease, rotation, revocation, scanner and break-glass outcomes shall emit metadata-only correlated ledger events.
observability_requirements.verification_method: Integration tests reconstruct an access decision and version lifecycle without retrieving secret material.

acceptance_criteria.title: Secret version persists without plaintext leakage
acceptance_criteria.given: An authorised Owner writes a secret version through approved provider adapter.
acceptance_criteria.then: AGASTYA stores only metadata, fingerprint and provider references; plaintext is absent from API, log and ledger fixtures.

acceptance_criteria.title: Agent-safe secret-backed tool execution
acceptance_criteria.given: An approved agent task requests a secret-backed registered tool operation.
acceptance_criteria.then: Agent sees no plaintext and registered tool receives only a short-lived bound materialisation lease.

acceptance_criteria.title: Plaintext export is denied
acceptance_criteria.given: Any normal user, API or agent path requests plaintext secret read or export.
acceptance_criteria.then: It is denied and audited without revealing recoverable secret information.

acceptance_criteria.title: Revocation blocks future grants
acceptance_criteria.then: The request is denied immediately and active lease outcome is recorded according to provider capability.

acceptance_criteria.title: Rotation preserves active secret on failure
acceptance_criteria.given: A registered rotation workflow creates a candidate version.
acceptance_criteria.then: Current active version remains active and a metadata-only failure event is recorded.

test_requirements.scope: Provider-adapter write and no-plaintext persistence/output controls.
test_requirements.expected_evidence: Redaction scan and encrypted-version metadata integration report.

test_requirements.scope: Opaque lease and direct registered tool materialisation for agent task.
test_requirements.expected_evidence: Task/tool trace proves no agent plaintext and correct bound lease attributes.

test_requirements.scope: Plaintext read/export, cross-project and unauthorised caller denials.
test_requirements.expected_evidence: API and UI negative-test report with metadata-only audit events.

test_requirements.scope: Version activation, rotation failure, retirement and emergency revocation.
test_requirements.expected_evidence: Lifecycle test report including active-lease decision after revocation.

risks.title: Incorrect provider integration weakens root-key boundary
risks.description: A poorly designed KMS/provider adapter could leak material or grant overly broad decryption authority.
risks.mitigation: Require approved provider ADR, adapter threat model, least-privilege identity and security review before ingestion.

open_questions.question: Which approved KMS/HSM or managed secret provider will be used in the initial environment?
open_questions.impact_if_unresolved: Credential ingestion and root-key boundary cannot be implemented.
open_questions.resolution: Accepted as a detailed-design risk. KMS/HSM or managed-provider selection is a mandatory security architecture gate before secret ingestion.

open_questions.question: What break-glass approver quorum, maximum lease TTL and review SLA apply per classification?
open_questions.resolution: Accepted as a detailed-design risk. Break-glass quorum, TTL and review policy must be approved before that capability is enabled.

architecture_decisions.title: Delegate cryptography and root-key operations to approved key-management provider
architecture_decisions.context: AGASTYA needs encrypted secret versions without owning root key material or custom cryptographic implementation.
architecture_decisions.decision: Use envelope encryption and an approved KMS/HSM or managed secret provider via a provider adapter; keep secret metadata separate from encrypted version material.

alternatives.name: Application-managed encryption keys
alternatives.summary: Generate and store root keys within AGASTYA application environment.
alternatives.rejection_reason: Expands key exposure and violates the desired independently governed root-key boundary.

architecture_decisions.rationale: A provider-managed root-key boundary allows least-privilege decryption, rotation, audit and security review.
consequences: No secret ingestion occurs before adapter and threat-model approval.

provenance.rationale: Implements agent tool governance requirement that agents never receive raw credentials.

coverage_summary.method: Initial vault draft mapping; implementation and runtime coverage are not applicable.
